title: Iff-split for IMO 2026 Q4: MulanCanGuarantee θ iff θ = 180/n
intent: Prove the headline iff of IMO 2026 Q4 by splitting it into its two directions with `constructor`; each direction is discharged by one project lemma stated and proved independently above it — the forward direction (⇒) by `exists_div_of_canGuarantee`, the backward direction (⇐) by `mulanCanGuarantee_of_div`.

parent.name: main_theorem
parent.statement:
theorem main_theorem (θ : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ180 : θ < 180) :
    MulanCanGuarantee θ ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ θ = 180 / n

children.name: exists_div_of_canGuarantee
children.statement:
lemma exists_div_of_canGuarantee {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ180 : θ < 180)
    (h : MulanCanGuarantee θ) : ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ θ = 180 / n
children.closed_by: rw [div_iff_intMul hθ0 hθ180]; by_contra hc; exact not_good_of_mulanWins hc (h _ htri) (good_equilateral hc)

children.name: mulanCanGuarantee_of_div
children.statement:
lemma mulanCanGuarantee_of_div {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {θ : ℝ} (hθdef : θ = 180 / n) :
    MulanCanGuarantee θ
children.closed_by: by_cases h : θ ∈ s; exact MulanWins.win h in the first case; else exact MulanWins.move hcut (mulanWins_of_succ_mul (theta_pos hn hθdef) i L hL hi) (mulanWins_of_succ_mul (theta_pos hn hθdef) j R hR hj) from the opening cut exists_opening_cut

applicability.goal_shape: An iff (Lean `↔`) whose two directions are already proved as separate lemmas: a forward lemma `hypothesis → conclusion` and a backward lemma `conclusion → hypothesis`. Same shape for order antisymmetry and set equality.
applicability.use_when: the two directions are genuinely different arguments (here a contradiction from a good equilateral triangle versus a constructive opening cut), each already stated as a self-contained lemma, so the glue is `constructor` plus one `exact` per side.
applicability.avoid_when: the two directions share most of their proof (fold them into one lemma, or use `le_antisymm`/`ext` directly); or a direction is not yet a lemma, in which case `constructor` just exposes an open goal and the split contributes nothing.

claims.claim: The parent `main_theorem` closes by `constructor`, which splits the iff into its two directions, and each bullet is a single `exact` application of a named project lemma — no tactic work happens inside the parent's proof.

The main proof is 4 lines of glue (lines 381-384) that call exactly 2 direct project lemmas; the two children's proofs are 6 and 7 lines (lines 365-370 and 273-279), and the longest chain of project lemmas below the main theorem is 5: main_theorem → exists_div_of_canGuarantee → not_good_of_mulanWins → good_of_cut → isTriangle_triple → card_triple.

claims.claim: The authors label this the 'Main theorem' and state the informal biconditional in the doc comment immediately above it, matching the formal statement line for line.

Each child is self-contained and closes on its own from named siblings, without referencing the other direction: exists_div_of_canGuarantee closes via not_good_of_mulanWins and good_equilateral (lines 363-370), and mulanCanGuarantee_of_div closes via exists_opening_cut and mulanWins_of_succ_mul (lines 271-279).

metrics.how_counted: parent proof = lines 381-384 of the copied file; child proofs = lines 365-370 (exists_div_of_canGuarantee) and 273-279 (mulanCanGuarantee_of_div); direct_children = the two lemmas named in the parent's proof

consequences: The split creates exactly two obligations, one per direction, both already discharged by named lemmas: (⇒) a guarantee forces θ = 180/n (by contradiction from the good equilateral triangle), and (⇐) θ = 180/n allows a guarantee (by a constructive opening cut). It also assigns each lemma exactly the hypotheses it needs — the forward direction requires 0 < θ and θ < 180, while the backward direction requires only 2 ≤ n and θ = 180/n. Failure mode: `constructor` on an iff whose sides are not lemmas merely exposes two open goals, so the split is worth recording only when the children already read on their own.
